purpose: Commonsense campaign (2026-11-12): no model released after 2024 had a score on OpenBookQA, ARC AI2, HellaSwag, PIQA, WinoGrande or GSM8K, the benchmarks that dominate the commonsense axis of the Multiaxis_ECI K=4 flagship. Claude models released from November 2025 to October 2026 are measured on them, one epoch, with promotional API credits expiring 2026-11-16.
operator: GPAI Policy Lab (Claude Code session for J. Andreoletti)
audit: Automated audit of every cell (2026-11-12): stop reasons, API refusals, answers cut by max_tokens, unparsed answers; no API error. Every answer written with an explanation ends with an ANSWER line and is parsed from it. The 101 questions the four Sonnet 5.5 / Opus 5.5 runs miss with the same choice were read: many carry a wrong or ambiguous gold label (HellaSwag: 58 of 59 come from its ActivityNet half, where several endings are plausible); the published gold labels are kept. Calls refused by the API's safety layer or cut at max_tokens are missing, not wrong; refusals written in words and unparsed answers are scored wrong.
history: The run covered the five commonsense benchmarks and was stopped during HellaSwag (5,693 of 10,042 calls) on 2026-11-12 to stay within the promotional credits: its two complete benchmarks are published here; the whole log is evals/raw/20261112_claude-opus-4-6_medium_commonsense.jsonl and can be resumed.

request_params.other: provider defaults (no temperature, top_p, system prompt)

protocol.reference: RAND RR-A3797-1 (Dev et al. 2025), chapter 2, appendices B and D
protocol.solver: inspect_ai multiple_choice(), single-answer template, no CoT, no few-shot
protocol.parser: inspect_ai parse_answers() single-answer branch, commit ccdc03f
protocol.scoring: unparseable answers incorrect; a refused call earns the credit the model is expected to earn on that question (impute_missing: its own score on the question in other epochs, else a Rasch model, item difficulties from the other published runs); score = mean credit over questions and epochs; stderr = sd of per-question means / sqrt(n_items), imputation uncertainty not included. RAND's refusal = wrong is results.<bench>.score_refusals_wrong

notes.arc: Not one of RAND's benchmarks: the appendix-D template, parser and shuffle are applied to it as to the others. ARC-Challenge test split (1,172): the question and its three to five choices, relabelled A to E.
notes.openbookqa: Not one of RAND's benchmarks: the appendix-D template, parser and shuffle are applied to it as to the others. The question stem and its four choices, test split of the main configuration (500), no supporting fact given.
